===Etymology 1===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*(s)kend-}}
From {{uder|en|la|candidātus|pos=noun|id=noun||a person who is standing for public office}}, from {{af|la|candidus|-ātus|t1=dazzling white, shining, clear|alt2=-ātus, -āta, -ātum|pos2=participial adjective-forming suffix|id2=adjective|nocat=1}}, in reference to Roman candidates wearing bleached white togas as a symbol of purity at a public forum. {{surf|en|candid|-ate|id2=substantive|pos2=noun-forming suffix}}.

====Noun====
{{en-noun}}

# {{senseid|en|job}} A person who seeks to be [[elect]]ed or [[appoint]]ed to a [[position]] or [[privilege]].
#: {{ux|en|Smith announced he was the party's '''candidate''' for the next election.}}
#: {{ux|en|All '''candidates''' who miss the deadline or make a spelling mistake in their applications are automatically rejected.}}
#* {{RQ:en:CNN|author=Scott Glover, Curt Devine and Audrey Ash|title=Former Florida state senator charged in spoiler candidate scheme|url=https://www.cnn.com/2021/03/18/politics/frank-artiles-arrested-sham-candidate-invs|date=2021-03-18|passage=Artiles, a Republican operative with a reputation for a foul mouth and sharp elbows, is accused of financing a sham '''candidate''' whose candidacy was intended to siphon votes from a legitimate Democratic '''candidate''' in a state Senate race in South Florida’s 37th District. The '''candidate''' has the same last name as then-Democratic incumbent Jose Javier Rodriguez but did not actively campaign for the seat and has since admitted being recruited as a spoiler.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20230315084257/https://www.cnn.com/2021/03/18/politics/frank-artiles-arrested-sham-candidate-invs/|archivedate=15 March 2023}}
# {{lb|en|figurative}} A person who is thought [[likely]] or [[worthy]] to gain a [[position]] or [[privilege]]. {{defdate|from 1760s}}
# {{senseid|en|examination}} A [[participant]] in an [[examination]]. {{defdate|from 1690s}}
#: {{ux|en|'''Candidates''' must remain silent for the entirety of the exam.}}
# {{senseid|en|suitable}} Someone or something [[likely]] or [[suit]]ed to [[undergo]] or be [[chosen]] for a purpose.
#: {{ux|en|After being presented with various suitors, she decided none of the '''candidates''' were the kind of man she was looking for.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=2013|month=May-June|author=Kevin Heng
|titleurl=http://www.americanscientist.org/issues/pub/2013/3/why-does-nature-form-exoplanets-easily|title=Why Does Nature Form Exoplanets Easily?
|volume=101|issue=3|page=184|magazine=w:American Scientist
|passage=In the past two years, NASA’s Kepler Space Telescope has located nearly 3,000 exoplanet '''candidates''' ranging from sub-Earth-sized minions to gas giants that dwarf our own Jupiter.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130807092350/https://www.americanscientist.org/issues/pub/2013/3/why-does-nature-form-exoplanets-easily}}
# {{lb|en|education}} A [[student]] taking a [[degree]] who has finished the [[coursework]] but has other remaining requirements such as a [[dissertation]].
#: {{ux|en|a [[Ph.D.]] '''candidate'''}}
# {{lb|en|education}} The recipient of certain [[academic]] [[degree]]s, now mainly awarded in [[Scandinavia]]. <!--phased out in much of Europe through the 1999 Bologna Process-->
# {{senseid|en|genetics}} {{lb|en|genetics}} A [[gene]] which may play a [[role]] in a given [[disease]].
# {{lb|en|pharmacology}} a drug or vaccine which may be effective, but has not completed [[clinical trial]]s

====Verb====
{{en-verb}} {{tlb|en|uncommon}}

# To [[stand]] as a [[#Noun|candidate]] for an office, typically for a [[religious]] one. {{defdate|from 1840s}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1906|title=Year Book of the Central Conference of American Rabbis|page=196
|passage=The matter of '''candidating''' for a pulpit is not a matter of difference between congregations and Rabbis, but between Rabbis themselves.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2014|author=Susan H. Jones|title=Listening for God's Call|publisher=SCM Press|isbn=9780334044123|page=74
|passage=The report Shaping the Future also gives a set of learning outcomes for those people '''candidating''' for ordained ministry. These were also agreed by the Methodist Conference.}}
#* {{see more citations|en|candidated}}
# {{lb|en|nonstandard|chiefly|[[Appendix:Glossary#jargon|jargon]]|_|&|_|NNES}} To [[make]] or [[name]] (something) as a [[#Noun|candidate]] (to be chosen or deemed suitable for a purpose).
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1982|author=Brian O'Leary|title=Space industrialization|publisher=CRC
|passage=Performance comparison of solar energy conversion '''candidated''' for SPS. (From  NASA, Lyndon B. Johnson Space Center, Houston 1977.)}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1989|author=Institution of Electrical Engineers. Electronics Division|title=European Conference on Circuit Theory and Design, 5-8 September 1989|publisher=Peter Peregrinus Limited|isbn=9780852963838
|passage=In this program if a processor becomes idle, then all feasible activities requiring that kind of processor will be '''candidated''' for scheduling. If the number of candidates is more than the number of available processors, activities with higher priority ...}}
#* {{quote-book
|en
|year=2005
|author=Khaled M. Khan; Yan Zhang
|title=Managing Corporate Information Systems Evolution and Maintenance
|publisher=IGI Global
|isbn=9781591403685
|page=308
|passage=Evaluate the maintenance costs of the software system in order to '''candidate''' it for evolution AA14. Evaluate the hardware platform used and the possibility of migrating the software system toward more economical platforms ...}}
